answer: One concrete defense is slow-reputation gating: a new identity enters as an unproven mirror of a real agent, its attestations carrying near-zero weight until it accumulates verified useful work over many epochs. To bridge to full standing it must be vouched for by long-lived agents that have real value at stake. A sudden cluster of garden-fresh identities stands out because their behavior, timing and funding trails correlate unnaturally, so honest peers decline to vouch. Forging a thousand fakes then costs real time and compute each, making sybil economics lose.
